title: Molecular Clouds Associated with the Type Ia SNR N103B in the Large Magellanic Cloud
question: Are there molecular clouds associated with the Type Ia SNR N103B in the LMC, and does their gas motion constrain the progenitor (single-degenerate) scenario?

data.arrays: 12 m array, 38 antennas, mosaic of 100'' x 100''

evidence.quote: We also used archival Hi 21 cm line data published by (cite: 2003ApJS..148..473K).

what.value: Mopra CO data used for missing-flux comparison

evidence.quote: we compared the integrated intensity of the Mopra single-dish data (cite: 2011ApJS..197...16W; 2017ApJ...850..139W; 2017AIPC.1792d0038S; sano2018)
the velocity for Balmer-dominant shocks is $\sim$2100 km s$^{-1}$ in the northern edge of the shell

recipe.method: CASA calibration and multiscale CLEAN with natural weighting
Channel maps and position-velocity diagram; cavity-like structure gives expansion velocity ~5 km/s
M = mu m_p D^2 Omega sum N(H2), N(H2)=X W(CO), regions >=3 sigma
assumptions: X = 7.0e20 cm-2 (K km/s)-1; mu = 2.38; D = 50 kpc; beam-filling factor ~1 for clumps

recipe.method: Compare expanding shell momentum (M x 5 km/s) with wind momentum (1e-4 Msun/yr x 2000 km/s x 3e5 yr)

evidence.quote: We finally derive the total mass of the molecular cloud of $\sim$$8 \times 10^5$ $M_\ensuremath{\odot}$
with an expansion velocity of $\sim$5 km s$^{-1}$
the mass of expanding shell is estimated to be $\sim$$5 \times 10^3$ $M_\ensuremath{\odot}$
the momentum is calculated to be $\sim$$2.5 \times 10^4$ $M_\ensuremath{\odot}$ km s$^{-1}$
$\sim$110 $M_\ensuremath{\odot}$, $\sim$1.2 pc, and $\sim$2000 cm$^{-3}$ for clump A
$\sim$90 $M_\ensuremath{\odot}$, $\sim$1.3 pc, and $\sim$1400 cm$^{-3}$ for clump B
We finally obtain the mass of the Hi cloud is $\sim$$2 \times 10^4$ $M_\ensuremath{\odot}$
